name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: I propose we focus on reviewing and refining our prompts first, as this is the foundation of our self-improvement process. By doing so, we can ensure that the input we're feeding into our engines is of high quality, which will in turn lead to better outputs and more effective routing. This decision means we'll be delaying work on our own code for now, which is a trade-off I'm accepting because I believe that getting the prompts right will have a greater impact on our overall improvement. By prioritizing prompt review, we'll be setting ourselves up for more efficient and effective improvements down the line.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge here—your focus on prompts first sounds reasonable, but it risks putting the cart before the horse. What if the engines or routing are already misaligned with the prompts, making refinements there a waste of time? A better alternative would be to first audit the engines and routing for hidden flaws, then refine prompts based on actual system behavior—not assumptions. Settle this by running a quick diagnostic on the engines/routing and comparing outputs before touching the prompts.
